main_text.p:
Non equidè dubito, quin primù inimica bonorù Lingua exectà auido sit data Vulturio.
Effossos oculos vocat atro gutture coruus,
Inteftina canes: cætera membra lupi.

At qui epiftolas fcribunt comminato-rias, moderationem adhibent: & nec le-ui mollíq; brachio cum improbis agunt: nec etiam nimis iifdem iralcitur & com-minantur. Collocatio verò & tractatio ita inftituitur: vt in exordio crimé ipfum cum querela & indignatione propona-tur: parte altera illud amplificetur atque exaggeretur: poftrema, vsɔɛɩ́ adhorta-tione, aut reprehenfione & comminatio-ne acri abfoluatur. De exemplis porrò & rebus ac materiis, quæ in comminatoriis eiufcemodi epiftolis tractantur, feorfim vt agamus, neceffe minimè habem9, pro-pterea quod ex reprehenforiis, expoftu-latoriis, querulis illæ fumi poffunt, quæ ita à Cicerone inftitui folent, vt territa-tiones & comminationes in fine habeât. Sunt etiam egregiæ multæ huius generis epiftolę in iis,quas Leonis pontificis no-mine ad diuerfos Bembus fcripfit: vt tamen etiam hic imitatio aliqua propo-natur.lib.5.epift.1.deligemus, in qua Ci-ceroni Metellus ob fratrem iniuria affe-

page.notes: Marginal notes (right margin, in order): "Collocatio et tractatio natoriarum epistolarum." (note beside "Collocatio verò"); "Res & materia communis natoriarum epistolarum." (note beside "De exemplis porrò"). Italic and Greek: the word beside "adhorta-tione" is printed in Greek letters (ἀποτρέπω-type word, partly illegible in the scan); transcribed as [illegible, ~7 letters] in the running text is avoided here, so the best reading is shown as "vsɔɛ" and marked uncertain: the Greek word "ἀποτροπή" is likely. Treat as [?]. The line "ita à Cicerone" and the word "neceffe minimè habem9" are as printed; "habem9" is a printing form for habemus. The footer "r 4" (signature mark, a gathering signature) is not transcribed. Several characters are uncertain due to scan quality; the Greek word after "poftrema," should be checked against the original.
